candidates.name: train_dedupe_chunks
candidates.note: RegexTokenizer.train keeps each distinct regex chunk once (first-seen order) with its multiplicity and counts pairs weighted. Pair counts and their first-seen order are unchanged, so max() picks the same merges, ties included.

ids = []
        # chunks repeat a lot in natural text (" the", ","): encode each distinct
        # chunk once per call
        cache = {}
        for chunk in text_chunks:
            chunk_ids = cache.get(chunk)
            if chunk_ids is None:
                chunk_bytes = chunk.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
                chunk_ids = cache[chunk] = self._encode_chunk(chunk_bytes)
            ids.extend(chunk_ids)
        return ids

candidates.name: decode_lookup_once
candidates.note: RegexTokenizer.decode looks each id up once (dict.get) instead of a membership test followed by an index, and binds the dict and the append method outside the loop. Same bytes, same error for an unknown id.
